raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
> **Draft.** Stacked on #43686 (packed varlen for `AITER_SAGE`). Depends on the gfx1201 SageAttention op in aiter: ROCm/aiter#6390 (HIP kernel), then a hand-scheduled code object as the follow-up. This PR stays a draft until those are merged. Until #43686 is merged, the diff here includes its commit; only the last commit belongs to this PR. Overall plan: [ROCm/aiter#6292](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6292#issuecomment-6106014448).

## Motivation

On Radeon RDNA4 (gfx1201: Radeon AI PRO R9700 / R9600D, Radeon RX 9070 series), `AITER_SAGE` runs aiter's Triton `fav3_sage` kernel, which is slower than BF16 SDPA. aiter is adding `aiter.gfx1201_sage_attention`, a SageAttention kernel written for gfx1201. It quantizes QK^T to INT8 and PV to FP8, accumulates in FP32, and takes BF16 `[B, S, H, 128]` input.

## Modifications

`AITERSageImpl` calls `aiter.gfx1201_sage_attention(q, k, v, softmax_scale=...)` when all of the following hold:

- the GPU is gfx1201;
- the installed aiter provides the op;
- the layer is non-causal, with `head_size == 128` and `num_kv_heads` equal to `num_heads`;
- the call has BF16 inputs, and Q/K/V have equal shapes.

Everything else keeps the existing `fav3_sage` kernel unchanged. That covers other GPUs (gfx942 / gfx950), other shapes or dtypes, cross-attention with different KV length, and aiter builds without the op. The layer's `softmax_scale` is now passed to the gfx1201 kernel. The `fav3_sage` call is unchanged. The first time the gfx1201 kernel is selected, one info line is logged.

Unit tests are in `test/unit/test_aiter_sage_attn_backend.py` and use a stubbed aiter, so they need no GPU. They check:

- that the gfx1201 kernel is selected and receives the softmax scale;
- that it is also used through `forward_varlen`;
- that every fallback case keeps `fav3_sage`.

## Accuracy and speed

**Kernel.** On a Radeon AI PRO R9700, `forward_varlen` matches direct per-segment `aiter.gfx1201_sage_attention` calls bitwise for trailing padding, multiple segments and a single segment, with both aiter part 1 (HIP) and part 2 (code object).

**End to end.** MiniMax-H3, with the case parameters of `minimax_h3_t2va_2gpu_h100`: t2va, 1344x768, 4 s, 8 steps, seed 42, TP2, on 2x R9700 (PyTorch 2.11 / ROCm 7.15). Same flags as that case. All rows include the fixes of #43686 (varlen, `causal` / `softmax_scale`, contiguous Q/K/V).

| attention | denoise stage | vs BF16 SDPA | video PSNR / audio cos vs SDPA run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `torch_sdpa` (BF16) | 152.3 s | 1.00x | - |
| `torch_sdpa`, K/V token order reversed (rounding-only noise floor) | 152.3 s | - | 34.41 dB / 0.991 |
| `aiter_sage` before this PR (`fav3_sage`, Triton) | 412.7 s | 0.37x | 26.42 dB / 0.68 |
| `aiter_sage`, this PR, aiter part 1 (HIP kernel) | 103.6 s | 1.47x | 33.47 dB / 0.958 |
| `aiter_sage`, this PR, aiter part 2 (code object) | 94.2 s | 1.62x | 32.14 dB / 0.897 |

On gfx1201, `AITER_SAGE` becomes 4.4x faster than with `fav3_sage`, and the video ends much closer to the BF16 run (32-33 dB vs. 26 dB, against a 34.4 dB rounding-only floor). On dumped MiniMax-H3 DiT inputs, the relative error vs. BF16 attention is 0.013 for the gfx1201 kernel and 0.054 for `fav3_sage`. The three Sage runs ran concurrently on separate GPU pairs, so their times vary by a few percent between repeats. The speedup is larger at longer sequences: on the 15 s / 362-frame ref2av case in LightX2V, the same kernel gives 211.6 -> 89.1 s per DiT step (2.38x).

The R9700 runs used `sgl-kernel` built for gfx1201 (#43679), and the custom all-reduce was disabled because R9700s connect over PCIe (#43676).

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed results (above).
- [ ] aiter part 1 (ROCm/aiter#6390) and part 2 merged; then mark ready for review.

nodes.body:
Note on run-to-run variation in the quality numbers above.

Repeating the same 8-step config (same seed, same tree) gives slightly different videos. For example, the asm path measured 32.84 dB in one run and 32.14 dB in another. We traced this down and it does **not** come from the attention kernels:

- `gfx1201_sage_attention` (asm and HIP) is bitwise deterministic: repeated calls on dirty memory, and 60 calls under concurrent side-stream load, give identical outputs.
- Hashing every DiT module across runs, the first divergence is in two **FP32 GEMMs** that are not part of this PR: the TimeEmbedder `proj_in` (`[1,256] x [2688,256]^T`) and the final-layer `video_out` (`[32704,5376] x [48,5376]^T`). Inputs, weights and bias are bitwise identical across runs, and recomputing in the same process gives the same result. Across processes, however, hipBLASLt/Tensile sometimes picks a different solution for the same shape, e.g. `MT16x8x64` vs `MT64x64x16`. In 12 runs, the output groups matched the kernel-name groups exactly. The 1-ulp difference is then amplified by the 50 DiT blocks over 8 steps.

So expect about ±0.7 dB PSNR jitter between identical runs on this stack, for every attention backend including SDPA. Only differences larger than that are meaningful. We are reproducing the per-process kernel choice standalone to report it to hipBLASLt.

Follow-up: the per-process kernel choice is a hipBLASLt bug. For untuned shapes, the heuristic falls back to a solution list ordered by host pointer value, so the kernel that runs depends on the heap layout. It is fixed on rocm-libraries `develop` (ROCm/rocm-libraries#11340) but not in any TheRock release yet. Reported with a standalone repro in ROCm/rocm-libraries#13476, with a backport to 10.1 in ROCm/rocm-libraries#13477.

@@ -1009,4 +1009,5 @@ sglang generate \
 ### Notes for ROCm / MPS
 
 - ROCm: use `--attention-backend torch_sdpa` or `fa` depending on what is available in your environment. On gfx1151 / Strix Halo (wave32), do **not** use `aiter` — prefer `torch_sdpa` (image sets `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`).
+- ROCm gfx1201 (Radeon AI PRO R9700 / R9600D, Radeon RX 9070): `aiter_sage` runs aiter's `gfx1201_sage_attention` kernel (INT8 QK^T, FP8 PV) for non-causal BF16 attention with head dim 128; other calls, and aiter builds without that op, keep the Triton `fav3_sage` kernel.
 - MPS: the platform implementation always uses `torch_sdpa`.

@@ -8,8 +8,27 @@
     AttentionImpl,
     AttentionMetadata,
     AttentionMetadataBuilder,
+    trailing_padding_used_len,
 )
-from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.platforms import AttentionBackendEnum
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.platforms import (
+    AttentionBackendEnum,
+    current_platform,
+)
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.utils.logging_utils import init_logger
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+def _gfx1201_sage_attention():
+    """aiter's SageAttention op for RDNA4 (gfx1201), or None on other GPUs."""
+    if not (
+        current_platform.is_rocm()
+        and current_platform.get_gcn_arch_name().startswith("gfx1201")
+    ):
+        return None
+    import aiter
+
+    return getattr(aiter, "gfx1201_sage_attention", None)
 
 
 class AITERSageBackend(AttentionBackend):
@@ -45,7 +64,20 @@ def __init__(
         dropout_p: float = 0.0,
         **extra_impl_args,
     ) -> None:
-
+        self.causal = causal
+        self.softmax_scale = softmax_scale
+        # The gfx1201 op covers non-causal BF16 attention with head_dim 128 and
+        # equal Q/K/V shapes; dtype and shapes are checked per call.
+        self.gfx1201_sage_attn_fn = (
+            _gfx1201_sage_attention()
+            if head_size == 128 and not causal and num_kv_heads in (None, num_heads)
+            else None
+        )
+        if self.gfx1201_sage_attn_fn is not None:
+            logger.info_once("AITER Sage: using aiter.gfx1201_sage_attention")
+        self.packed_trailing_padding = extra_impl_args.get(
+            "packed_trailing_padding", False
+        )
         try:
             from aiter.ops.triton.attention.fav3_sage import fav3_sage_wrapper_func
 
@@ -75,5 +107,66 @@ def forward(
             Output tensor of shape [batch_size, seq_len, head_num, head_dim]
         """
 
-        output = self.aiter_sage_attn_fn(query, key, value)
+        if (
+            self.gfx1201_sage_attn_fn is not None
+            and query.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+            and key.shape == query.shape
+            and value.shape == query.shape
+        ):
+            return self.gfx1201_sage_attn_fn(
+                query.contiguous(),
+                key.contiguous(),
+                value.contiguous(),
+                softmax_scale=self.softmax_scale,
+            )
+        # aiter's Sage quantization assumes dense inputs; strided views such as
+        # slices of a fused QKV projection give wrong results (ROCm/aiter#6222).
+        output = self.aiter_sage_attn_fn(
+            query.contiguous(),
+            key.contiguous(),
+            value.contiguous(),
+            softmax_scale=self.softmax_scale,
+            causal=self.causal,
+        )
+        return output
+
+    def forward_varlen(
+        self,
+        query: torch.Tensor,
+        key: torch.Tensor,
+        value: torch.Tensor,
+        *,
+        cu_seqlens: torch.Tensor,
+        max_seqlen: int,
+        cu_seqlens_host: tuple[int, ...] | None = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Packed varlen attention: [total_tokens, head_num, head_dim] in and out,
+        one kernel call per segment of ``cu_seqlens``."""
+        bounds = tuple(
+            cu_seqlens_host
+            if cu_seqlens_host is not None
+            else (int(x) for x in cu_seqlens.tolist())
+        )
+        # MiniMax-H3 packs one live document as bounds=(0, used, total):
+        # [0, used) are real tokens; [used, total) is 64-aligned tail padding.
+        if self.packed_trailing_padding:
+            used = trailing_padding_used_len(
+                total_tokens=query.shape[0], max_seqlen=max_seqlen, bounds=bounds
+            )
+            if used is not None:
+                bounds = (0, used)
+        if bounds == (0, query.shape[0]):
+            return self.forward(
+                query.unsqueeze(0), key.unsqueeze(0), value.unsqueeze(0)
+            )[0]
+        # Keep padded tail rows at zero so downstream masked rows stay inactive.
+        output = torch.zeros_like(query)
+        for start, stop in zip(bounds[:-1], bounds[1:]):
+            if start == stop:
+                continue
+            output[start:stop] = self.forward(
+                query[start:stop].unsqueeze(0),
+                key[start:stop].unsqueeze(0),
+                value[start:stop].unsqueeze(0),
+            )[0]
         return output

@@ -0,0 +1,185 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""AITER Sage backend: kernel arguments, gfx1201 kernel selection and packed varlen (no GPU or aiter needed)."""
+
+import sys
+import types
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+MODULE = "sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.layers.attention.backends.aiter_sage"
+
+
+class _Calls(list):
+    kwargs: list
+    contiguous: list
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def calls(monkeypatch):
+    """Stub aiter's kernels; record (kernel, sequence length[, softmax_scale]) and fav3 kwargs."""
+    calls = _Calls()
+    calls.kwargs = []
+    calls.contiguous = []
+
+    def gfx1201_sage_attention(q, k, v, softmax_scale=None):
+        calls.append(("gfx1201", q.shape[1], softmax_scale))
+        return q + 1
+
+    def fav3_sage_wrapper_func(q, k, v, softmax_scale=None, causal=False):
+        calls.append(("fav3", q.shape[1]))
+        calls.kwargs.append({"softmax_scale": softmax_scale, "causal": causal})
+        calls.contiguous.append(all(t.is_contiguous() for t in (q, k, v)))
+        return q + 2
+
+    aiter = types.ModuleType("aiter")
+    aiter.gfx1201_sage_attention = gfx1201_sage_attention
+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "aiter", aiter)
+    fav3 = types.ModuleType("aiter.ops.triton.attention.fav3_sage")
+    fav3.fav3_sage_wrapper_func = fav3_sage_wrapper_func
+    for name in ("aiter.ops", "aiter.ops.triton", "aiter.ops.triton.attention"):
+        monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, name, types.ModuleType(name))
+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, fav3.__name__, fav3)
+    return calls
+
+
+def _impl(monkeypatch, arch="gfx942", *, head_size=128, causal=False, **extra):
+    from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.layers.attention.backends.aiter_sage import (
+        AITERSageImpl,
+    )
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(f"{MODULE}.current_platform.is_rocm", lambda: True)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        f"{MODULE}.current_platform.get_gcn_arch_name",
+        lambda: arch,
+        raising=False,
+    )
+    return AITERSageImpl(
+        num_heads=4,
+        head_size=head_size,
+        softmax_scale=0.125,
+        causal=causal,
+        **extra,
+    )
+
+
+def test_forward_passes_softmax_scale_and_causal(monkeypatch, calls):
+    q, k, v = (torch.randn(1, 16, 4, 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16) for _ in range(3))
+    _impl(monkeypatch).forward(q, k, v)
+    _impl(monkeypatch, "gfx1201", causal=True).forward(q, k, v)
+    assert calls == [("fav3", 16), ("fav3", 16)]
+    assert calls.kwargs == [
+        {"softmax_scale": 0.125, "causal": False},
+        {"softmax_scale": 0.125, "causal": True},
+    ]
+
+
+def test_forward_makes_strided_inputs_contiguous(calls, monkeypatch):
+    qkv = torch.randn(1, 16, 3 * 4 * 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    q, k, v = (t.view(1, 16, 4, 128) for t in qkv.split(4 * 128, dim=-1))
+    assert not v.is_contiguous()
+    out = _impl(monkeypatch).forward(q, k, v)
+    assert calls.contiguous == [True]
+    assert torch.equal(out, q + 2)
+
+
+def _packed_qkv(tokens):
+    return [torch.randn(tokens, 4, 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16) for _ in range(3)]
+
+
+def test_backend_supports_packed_varlen():
+    from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.layers.attention.backends.aiter_sage import (
+        AITERSageBackend,
+    )
+
+    assert AITERSageBackend.supports_packed_varlen()
+
+
+def test_forward_varlen_runs_each_segment(monkeypatch, calls):
+    q, k, v = _packed_qkv(10)
+    out = _impl(monkeypatch).forward_varlen(
+        q, k, v, cu_seqlens=torch.tensor([0, 3, 3, 10]), max_seqlen=7
+    )
+    assert calls == [("fav3", 3), ("fav3", 7)]
+    assert torch.equal(out, q + 2)
+
+
+def test_forward_varlen_single_segment(monkeypatch, calls):
+    q, k, v = _packed_qkv(10)
+    out = _impl(monkeypatch).forward_varlen(
+        q,
+        k,
+        v,
+        cu_seqlens=torch.tensor([0, 10]),
+        max_seqlen=10,
+        cu_seqlens_host=[0, 10],
+    )
+    assert calls == [("fav3", 10)]
+    assert torch.equal(out, q + 2)
+
+
+def test_forward_varlen_skips_trailing_padding(monkeypatch, calls):
+    q, k, v = _packed_qkv(10)
+    out = _impl(monkeypatch, packed_trailing_padding=True).forward_varlen(
+        q, k, v, cu_seqlens=torch.tensor([0, 6, 10]), max_seqlen=6
+    )
+    assert calls == [("fav3", 6)]
+    assert torch.equal(out[:6], q[:6] + 2)
+    assert not out[6:].any()
+
+
+def test_forward_varlen_without_padding_flag_runs_the_tail_segment(monkeypatch, calls):
+    q, k, v = _packed_qkv(10)
+    _impl(monkeypatch).forward_varlen(
+        q, k, v, cu_seqlens=torch.tensor([0, 6, 10]), max_seqlen=6
+    )
+    assert calls == [("fav3", 6), ("fav3", 4)]
+
+
+def test_gfx1201_uses_the_gfx1201_kernel_with_the_softmax_scale(monkeypatch, calls):
+    q, k, v = (torch.randn(1, 16, 4, 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16) for _ in range(3))
+    out = _impl(monkeypatch, "gfx1201").forward(q, k, v)
+    assert calls == [("gfx1201", 16, 0.125)]
+    assert torch.equal(out, q + 1)
+
+
+def test_gfx1201_packed_varlen_uses_the_gfx1201_kernel(monkeypatch, calls):
+    q, k, v = _packed_qkv(10)
+    impl = _impl(monkeypatch, "gfx1201", packed_trailing_padding=True)
+    impl.forward_varlen(q, k, v, cu_seqlens=torch.tensor([0, 6, 10]), max_seqlen=6)
+    assert calls == [("gfx1201", 6, 0.125)]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "arch, head_size, causal, num_kv_heads, dtype, kv_tokens",
+    [
+        ("gfx942", 128, False, None, torch.bfloat16, 16),
+        ("gfx950", 128, False, None, torch.bfloat16, 16),
+        ("gfx1201", 64, False, None, torch.bfloat16, 16),
+        ("gfx1201", 128, True, None, torch.bfloat16, 16),
+        ("gfx1201", 128, False, 2, torch.bfloat16, 16),
+        ("gfx1201", 128, False, None, torch.float16, 16),
+        ("gfx1201", 128, False, None, torch.bfloat16, 24),
+    ],
+)
+def test_other_cases_keep_the_triton_kernel(
+    monkeypatch, calls, arch, head_size, causal, num_kv_heads, dtype, kv_tokens
+):
+    q = torch.randn(1, 16, 4, head_size).to(dtype)
+    k, v = (torch.randn(1, kv_tokens, 4, head_size).to(dtype) for _ in range(2))
+    impl = _impl(
+        monkeypatch, arch, head_size=head_size, causal=causal, num_kv_heads=num_kv_heads
+    )
+    impl.forward(q, k, v)
+    assert calls == [("fav3", 16)]
+
+
+def test_gfx1201_without_the_aiter_op_keeps_the_triton_kernel(monkeypatch, calls):
+    del sys.modules["aiter"].gfx1201_sage_attention
+    q, k, v = (torch.randn(1, 16, 4, 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16) for _ in range(3))
+    _impl(monkeypatch, "gfx1201").forward(q, k, v)
+    assert calls == [("fav3", 16)]
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))

issue_comments.body:
Note on run-to-run variation in the quality numbers above.

Repeating the same 8-step config (same seed, same tree) gives slightly different videos. For example, the asm path measured 32.84 dB in one run and 32.14 dB in another. We traced this down and it does **not** come from the attention kernels:

- `gfx1201_sage_attention` (asm and HIP) is bitwise deterministic: repeated calls on dirty memory, and 60 calls under concurrent side-stream load, give identical outputs.
- Hashing every DiT module across runs, the first divergence is in two **FP32 GEMMs** that are not part of this PR: the TimeEmbedder `proj_in` (`[1,256] x [2688,256]^T`) and the final-layer `video_out` (`[32704,5376] x [48,5376]^T`). Inputs, weights and bias are bitwise identical across runs, and recomputing in the same process gives the same result. Across processes, however, hipBLASLt/Tensile sometimes picks a different solution for the same shape, e.g. `MT16x8x64` vs `MT64x64x16`. In 12 runs, the output groups matched the kernel-name groups exactly. The 1-ulp difference is then amplified by the 50 DiT blocks over 8 steps.

So expect about ±0.7 dB PSNR jitter between identical runs on this stack, for every attention backend including SDPA. Only differences larger than that are meaningful. We are reproducing the per-process kernel choice standalone to report it to hipBLASLt.

Follow-up: the per-process kernel choice is a hipBLASLt bug. For untuned shapes, the heuristic falls back to a solution list ordered by host pointer value, so the kernel that runs depends on the heap layout. It is fixed on rocm-libraries `develop` (ROCm/rocm-libraries#11340) but not in any TheRock release yet. Reported with a standalone repro in ROCm/rocm-libraries#13476, with a backport to 10.1 in ROCm/rocm-libraries#13477.
